clue.text: Record time

definitions.meaning: the written record of a meeting's proceedings
a measure of time, sixty seconds apiece

explanation.surface: A runner sets a record time.
explanation.definitionFit: The official record of a meeting and short spans of a clock's hour share this one plural word.

clue.text: My holding tie-ring broken in half

indicators.note: the first word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: a broken thing falls apart, so the letters of tie are rearranged

explanation.surface: My tie-ring has broken in half.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR printed 'tic-ring'; the page means tie-ring. 'Broken in half' tempts as the anagram phrase, but 'in half' is the definition with a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal and literary term for one of two equal parts of something.

clue.text: Captures the realm with eastern ornament

parts.note: nets means catches or captures
the realm is the United Kingdom, UK

explanation.surface: A conqueror seizes the kingdom along with an oriental trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: A small carved Japanese toggle, often ivory, worn on a sash and prized as a decorative collectable.

clue.text: 'It's not murder, anyhow, getting a military beating

indicators.note: anyhow means in any haphazard fashion, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier insists a brutal beating was not murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow' signals an anagram of NOT MURDER. The definition is cryptic: the instrument is the thing beaten in military bands.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum pitched between snare and bass, used in military and pipe bands, is something beaten.

clue.text: Be bright — and wicked until eight, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so it only has to sound right

parts.note: sin is wickedness; till means until; the number spelt out

explanation.surface: Be lively and stay up being wicked until eight o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'sin till eight' sounds like the answer. The OCR text was garbled; the printed page reads 'Be bright' and 'eight'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle or be dazzlingly clever and witty.

clue.text: Appropriate country for 17 on a luxury cruise ?

definitions.text: Appropriate country for 17 on a luxury cruise ?

parts.words: Appropriate country for 17 on a luxury cruise ?
parts.note: a cruise passenger who lives in the lap of luxury comes ashore (17, going ashore, means to land), so the fitting country joins those two ideas

explanation.surface: A travel writer suggests where passengers on a luxury cruise might best step ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lap of luxury' is the idiom behind the first half; 17-across is going ashore, which is to land. Put together they name the northern region of Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: The far-northern region of Finland, Sweden and Norway, home of the Sami, counts as a country in the old loose sense of a land.

clue.text: Pull Jock's ear

definitions.meaning: Jock is a stock Scotsman, so this is the Scots dialect word for the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone tugs a Scotsman's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a traditional nickname for a Scot, and LUG is Scots for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something heavy, and a Scottish word for an ear.

clue.text: Leave on deposit a fur jacket

parts.note: to park something is to leave it somewhere for a time, as money is parked on deposit

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a fur jacket with the bank as security.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded windproof coat, originally of animal skin, from the Arctic.

clue.text: Slander, like, intrinsically

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
per se is Latin for in itself, intrinsically

explanation.surface: A defamatory remark that is slanderous by its very nature.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread damaging falsehoods about someone, to cast a slur on them.

clue.text: Minds may turn to this theory of the universe

indicators.note: to turn the words over is to rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: Thinkers may be drawn to this cosmology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' signals an anagram of MINDS MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophical system explaining all phenomena as the action of forces rather than inert matter.

clue.text: Meaning careful work by a stay-at-home sister?

parts.note: a sister staying at home is in, not out
tending is looking after someone carefully, as a nursing sister does

explanation.surface: A nurse who never goes out does her careful work at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' hints at a nursing sister, whose careful work is tending patients; being at home is being 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning to do something is having the purpose or plan to do it.

clue.text: Full speed ahead in North Yorkshire

definitions.meaning: to let something ... is to carry on at full tilt
a cathedral city located in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A driver goes flat out through the Yorkshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPON is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England, known for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting it rip and carrying on is going headlong; the same letters name a cathedral city in that English county.

clue.text: Nothing's —— than taxes, said Barkis

parts.note: a quotation to complete: Barkis, the carrier in Dickens's David Copperfield, says something is as true as taxes, and nothing more so

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: Barkis, the carrier who courts Peggotty in David Copperfield, says it is as true as taxes is, and nothing is more so than them.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning certain or accurate completes the carrier's homely saying.

clue.text: Four-letter word caused great embarrassment in old transport

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a tram is a street vehicle of the old days on rails

indicators.note: embarrassment throws things into disorder, so the letters of great are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone swore on an old tram and caused great embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' suggests swearing, which fits the embarrassment on the tram, but here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek tetra means four and gramma a letter, so the word names any word of four letters, especially the Hebrew name of God.

clue.text: Slim ruler-capital aid to concentration

parts.note: thin means slim
a king is a ruler
cap is short for a capital letter

explanation.surface: A slender monarch of the capital helps people focus.
explanation.definitionFit: A notional hat one puts on to think hard, an idiom for applying the mind.

clue.text: With their spirit they can be match-savers

definitions.text: With their spirit they can be match-savers

parts.words: With their spirit they can be match-savers
parts.note: devices fuelled with spirit that light cigarettes, so smokers need not use up matches

explanation.surface: Spirited players can save a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'match-savers' suggest a plucky team rescuing a game; the spirit is fuel and the matches are the kind you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette lighters running on volatile fuel replace the need for struck matches.

clue.text: They don't make for relaxation on the cat-walk

definitions.text: They don't make for relaxation on the cat-walk

parts.words: They don't make for relaxation on the cat-walk
parts.note: millinery feats shown by models on a fashion runway, but read as cricket's triple dismissals that give a batting side no rest

explanation.surface: Fashion models find the runway anything but relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a hat trick is three wickets from three consecutive balls; the cat-walk adds the image of models showing off hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Three successes in a row, as in taking three wickets with consecutive deliveries, punned as stunts with headgear.

clue.text: There's money in Eastern gold, teacher

indicators.note: the money word sits inside the other letters

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a ducat is an old gold coin

explanation.surface: A teacher is paid in eastern gold.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instructs others, a schoolmaster or tutor.

clue.text: One boatman risked trouble, going ashore

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A boatman risked trouble when he went ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' signals an anagram of I (one), BOATMAN and RISKED, fourteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a ship or boat for dry land is the process of stepping off it.

clue.text: Herb-Roberts? No, Peter's

parts.note: herb-Robert and St Peter's wort are both medicinal plants of the old herbalists

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a guess about whose herbs these are.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lost its letter count in the OCR; it is (7). Herb-Robert is a wild geranium and St Peter's wort a hypericum, both old remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal plants used singly as remedies were known by this old herbalists' term.

clue.text: Away team In wrong position

parts.note: off means away
a side is a team

explanation.surface: The visiting team's player was caught in the wrong position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away team' suggests the visitors in a football match, which fits the offside rule in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead of the ball illegally in football or rugby, so out of a permitted place.

clue.text: Joins the passing-out parade? Only pretends

definitions.meaning: a pun on someone fainting, one who passes out
makes deceptive moves, as a boxer does

explanation.surface: A recruit only pretends to take part in the graduation parade.
explanation.walkthrough: A passing-out parade marks the end of military training; passing out is also fainting, a word pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretended attacks or deceptive movements meant to throw an opponent off guard.

clue.text: All washed up? Then confess!

definitions.meaning: humorously, to have become spotless after a wash

explanation.surface: Someone whose career is over is urged to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up is an idiom built on emerging spotless, which is also a jokey reading of being thoroughly washed.

clue.text: Scotland's river has title role in 'Sixties film

definitions.meaning: Bonnie and ... (1967), the gangster film named after its two outlaws

explanation.surface: A Scottish river has a starring part in a film of the sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow's river shares its name with the male outlaw played by Warren Beatty in the 1967 film.

clue.text: Plunder — some foresight needed for this

definitions.meaning: a gun has a foresight, the sighting blade at the muzzle

explanation.surface: Looting requires some forward planning.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is one sense; the other is a firearm, aimed with a foresight at its muzzle.

clue.text: Match score

explanation.surface: The result of a football game.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond with something and a running count of points are both this one word.

clue.text: Extract from boiling cod, once it has been cooked

indicators.note: cooked as in cooking the books, falsified, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fish stock is made by boiling cod once it has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has been cooked' signals an anagram of COD, ONCE and IT; the fish stock picture hides that the extract is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid concentrate made by simmering a substance in water to draw out its essence.

clue.text: Underworld boss in the Leeward Islands

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: A gangster runs things in the Caribbean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, also Dante's name for Satan's city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman ruler of the dead, Dis Pater, equivalent of Pluto.

clue.text: Apples from old country places

parts.note: rus is the Latin word for the countryside, hence old
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Apples come from orchards in old country places.
explanation.walkthrough: RUS is Latin for the countryside, the source of 'rustic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of rough-skinned brownish eating varieties grown in English orchards.

clue.text: Successful examinees can't answer all the questions

definitions.meaning: candidates who get through a test
a quiz contestant who cannot answer says pass

explanation.surface: Those who do well in a test still can't answer everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates who get through a test, and contestants who say pass when stumped by a question.
